h a coastline stretching for more than 100,000 kilometers, including its islands and fjords, Norway has developed deep expertise in the complex ocean and energy industries. 
For generations, the sea has shaped Norway's economy and identity, giving the country deep expertise in shipping, offshore industries and ocean technologies.
China, meanwhile, has emerged as a global industrial powerhouse, leading the world in shipbuilding and playing a major role in energy and advanced manufacturing.
As these industries become greener and smarter, demand is growing for new technologies and specialized expertise.
For Norway, this opens a new avenue for cooperation with China, bringing not only products, but also knowledge, technology and digital solutions developed through decades of experience in demanding ocean and energy industries.
That opportunity comes into focus this year at the China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), where Norway is the Guest Country of Honor. The event runs from September 9 to 13 in Beijing.
At its national pavilion, Norwegian companies showcase services and solutions focusing on green energy, digital technology, healthy living products and premium nutrition.
The ambition goes beyond selling individual products. Henning Kristoffersen, commercial counsellor at the Norwegian Embassy in China and director of Innovation Norway China, said Norwegian companies hope to move from offering individual products to providing more comprehensive solutions, and from one-off transactions to long-term cooperation.
China is Norway's most important trading partner in Asia. Kristoffersen said the two countries have complementary strengths in areas including maritime industries, energy and sustainable development, while the CIFTIS offers a platform for Norwegian companies to expand their business networks and build long-term partnerships.
Greener shipping
For DNV, a Norwegian-founded risk management company, that cooperation has been taking shape for more than a century.
It has had a presence in China for nearly 140 years, and its relationship with China's maritime industry began with ship inspection and classification in 1888. It provided independent technical assessments to help ensure that vessels meet required standards.
Today, however, this partnership extends far beyond inspecting ships. As international laws are demanding the ship industry searches for ways to cut emissions, and financiers are also paying greater attention to the environmental performance of vessels, DNV is increasingly working with Chinese shipbuilders and shipowners on designing and building the next generation of vessels.
But the path toward greener shipping is far from straightforward. There is no single alternative fuel suitable for every vessel and every shipping route. The choice depends on factors including the type of ship, where it operates and whether a particular fuel is available along its route.
That uncertainty creates both technological and financial risks. Many companies have adopted a cautious approach, building conventional vessels while leaving room for future retrofitting.
Chinese shipbuilders and shipowners, however, are increasingly moving directly toward vessels designed to use alternative fuels, according to Norbert Kray, senior vice president and regional manager for Greater China at DNV.
This is where DNV says it can play a role. The company is working with Chinese clients earlier in the process, providing technical expertise, data and analysis to help them assess different technological options. It helps companies navigate uncertainty as they transition to greener shipping.
Kray said China's influence on the global transformation of shipping is significant. As Chinese shipbuilders receive more orders for vessels designed to meet new environmental requirements, decisions made in Chinese shipyards are gradually shaping the future of the global maritime industry.
If DNV illustrates how a traditional maritime service is evolving to meet the demands of greener shipping, Falkor, a company developing industrial software and digital solutions formerly known as Kongsberg Digital, illustrates another direction: the growing role of digital services in managing complex industrial operations.
Deep Sea No. 1 (Shenhai-1), China's first independently operated deepwater gas field, lies beneath the South China Sea. At peak production, the field can supply more than 3 billion cubic meters of natural gas a year, providing energy for about 21 million people.
Operating a gas field deep beneath the surface leads to challenges that are difficult to see and even harder to manage.
On the seabed, temperatures can fall to around 3 degrees Celsius. Low temperatures, combined with the mixture of gas, water and other fluids moving through subsea pipelines, can create risks including hydrate formation and unstable flow.
In such an environment, operators cannot simply wait for something to go wrong before responding.
This is where the Norwegian company steps in, using a digital model to create a virtual representation of the gas field's highly complex physical operations.
This can simulate different operating conditions, collect data and give engineers a clearer picture of the operation, helping them make decisions before problems arise.
It can also support decisions about pipeline cleaning, optimize operating parameters and analyze energy consumption.
Sorting salmon
The broader shift in China-Norway cooperation can be seen not only in large industrial projects, but also in efforts to address environmental challenges.
Norway is home to countless rivers where wild Atlantic salmon migrate upstream to spawn. But the country's wild salmon populations have faced growing pressure in recent decades, from invasive humpback, or pink salmon that compete with native fish for habitat and food, and also climate change and human activity.
According to the Norwegian Environment Agency, more than 480,000 pink salmon were caught or observed in Norwegian rivers in 2023, exceeding the number of wild Atlantic salmon that returned to Norway's rivers to spawn in 2024.
Removing the invasive fish has traditionally relied heavily on volunteers, a labor-intensive process which has been made more difficult by the challenge of identifying fish as they move underwater.
In 2021, Huawei Norway joined with Norwegian technology partners to develop an AI-powered fish trap to help address the problem.
For the first year, a system using an underwater camera and machine vision was tested in the Storelva River near Berlevag, northern Norway, to identify different fish species as they passed through the trap.
Trained on tens of thousands of images, the AI system learned to distinguish native Atlantic salmon from invasive pink salmon in real time, with an accuracy of more than 90%.
Since 2022, a sorting system designed to distinguish between wild salmon and invasive pink salmon has been installed downstream in the Storelva River, before it reaches the sea.
Once a fish is identified, the system opens the gate for native salmon, allowing them to continue upstream to spawn, while diverting invasive pink salmon into nearby holding tanks for removal.
Tor Schulstad, administrator of the hunting and fishing association Berlevag JFF in Norway, said native salmon face critical challenges from invasive pink salmon and escaped farmed salmon, while the monitoring systems using AI is helping to stop this and enable future-proof river management.
In the summer time last year, the system helped intercept more than 4,000 invasive pink salmon in the Skallelv River, easing the pressure on native species.
Services cooperation
These examples illustrate cooperation is no longer limited to the exchange of products. It increasingly involves knowledge, technology and specialized services, with companies from both countries bringing different strengths to address specific needs.
The CIFTIS has become a forum for companies to understand where to find common ground, connecting expertise and technology with China's industrial scale and growing demand for advanced solutions.
This year, the CIFTIS is bringing together more than 1,800 companies from around 90 countries and international organizations, showcasing new technologies, solutions and achievements across a range of fast-growing fields, from high-tech and fintech to smart healthcare.
Around 100 promotional events and business negotiations are also scheduled, giving companies from around the world an opportunity to explore partnerships and turn new ideas into practical cooperation.

这种不确定性带来了技术和金融双重风险。许多企业采取了谨慎的做法，建造传统船舶的同时为未来改装留出空间。然而，据DNV高级副总裁兼大中华区区域经理诺伯特·克雷介绍，中国造船企业和船东正越来越多地直接转向设计使用替代燃料的船舶。DNV表示这正是其可以发挥作用的领域。该公司在流程更早的阶段就与中国客户合作，提供技术专长、数据和分析，帮助他们评估不同的技术方案。

它帮助企业在向绿色航运转型的过程中应对不确定性。克雷表示，中国对全球航运转型的影响力举足轻重。随着中国造船企业获得更多符合新环保要求船舶的订单，中国船厂做出的决策正在逐步塑造全球海事产业的未来。如果说DNV展示了传统海事服务如何演变以满足绿色航运的需求，那么Falkor——一家开发工业软件和数字解决方案的公司，前身为康士伯数字——则展示了另一个方向：数字服务在管理复杂工业运营中日益重要的作用。深海一号

（Shenhai-1）是中国首个自主运营的深水气田，位于南海海底。在产量高峰期，该气田每年可供应超过30亿立方米天然气，为约2100万人提供能源。在海底深处运营气田会带来难以察觉、更难以管理的挑战。在海底，温度可降至约3摄氏度。低温加上天然气、水和其他流体在海底管道中流动的混合物，可能产生水合物形成和流动不稳定等风险。

在这样的环境中，运营方不能等到出了问题才做出反应。这正是这家挪威公司介入的地方，它使用数字模型创建气田高度复杂的物理运营的虚拟表示。这可以模拟不同的运营条件，收集数据，让工程师更清晰地了解运营情况，帮助他们在问题出现之前做出决策。它还可以支持管道清洁决策、优化运营参数和分析能耗。分拣三文鱼——中挪合作的更广泛转变不仅体现在大型工业项目中，也体现在应对环境挑战的努力中。

挪威拥有无数河流，野生大西洋鲑鱼洄游上游产卵。但近几十年来，该国野生鲑鱼种群面临越来越大的压力，来自入侵的驼背鲑（粉鲑）与本地鱼类争夺栖息地和食物，以及气候变化和人类活动的影响。据挪威环境署统计，2023年在挪威河流中捕获或观测到的粉鲑超过48万条，超过了2024年返回挪威河流产卵的野生大西洋鲑数量。清除入侵鱼类传统上严重依赖志愿者，这是一个劳动密集型的过程，而识别水下移动鱼类的难度使这一工作更加困难。2021年，华为挪威公司与挪威技术合作伙伴联手开发了一种人工智能驱动的鱼陷阱来帮助解决这一问题。

第一年，一套使用水下摄像头和机器视觉的系统在挪威北部贝勒沃格附近的斯托尔瓦河进行了测试，用于在鱼类通过陷阱时识别不同鱼种。经过数万张图像的训练，该AI系统学会了实时区分本地大西洋鲑和入侵粉鲑，准确率超过90%。自2022年以来，一套旨在区分野生鲑鱼和入侵粉鲑的分拣系统已安装在斯托尔瓦河下游、入海之前。一旦识别出鱼类，系统便为本地鲑鱼打开闸门，让它们继续上游产卵，同时将入侵粉鲑引入附近的暂养池进行清除。挪威贝勒沃格狩猎和钓鱼协会管理员托尔·舒尔斯塔德表示，本地鲑鱼面临入侵粉鲑和逃逸养殖鲑鱼的严峻挑战，而使用AI的监测系统正在帮助阻止这一趋势，实现面向未来的河流管理。

去年夏天，该系统在斯卡勒尔夫河帮助拦截了4000多条入侵粉鲑，减轻了本地物种的压力。服务合作——这些例子表明，合作不再局限于产品交换。它越来越多地涉及知识、技术和专业服务，两国企业带来不同的优势以满足特定需求。服贸会已成为企业了解在哪里找到共同点的论坛，将专业知识和技术与中国的工业规模和对先进解决方案日益增长的需求对接。今年，服贸会汇聚了来自约90个国家和国际组织的1800多家企业，展示从高科技和金融科技到智慧医疗等一系列快速增长领域的新技术、新解决方案和新成果。

约100场推介活动和商务洽谈也已排定，为来自世界各地的企业提供了探索伙伴关系、将新想法转化为实际合作的机会。

articles.title: Why 'red tourism' is winning over China's younger generation
articles.titleCn: 为什么“红色旅游”正在赢得中国年轻一代的青睐
articles.summary: For many young Chinese, revolutionary history is no longer something to be read about in textbooks or viewed from behind glass. It is becoming an experience — one that can involve walking through historic sites, taking on a role in a wartime scenario or even stepping into a virtual recreation of the Long March.
articles.summaryCn: 红色旅游在中国年轻人中日益流行，沉浸式体验和数字技术让革命历史变得可参与、可感知，而其深层吸引力在于年轻人对意义、责任与文化自信的追寻。

paragraphs.en: Visitors view an exhibition featuring archival documents and photographs about the Red Army's Long March through Yunnan Province at the Kunming Museum in Kunming, southwest China's Yunnan Province, September 12, 2026. For many young Chinese, the Communist Party of China's (CPC) {{0}} history is no longer just something to be read about in textbooks or viewed from behind glass. It is becoming an experience — one that can involve walking through historic sites, taking on a role in a wartime scenario or even stepping into a virtual recreation of the Long March. That {{1}} is helping fuel a new wave of "red tourism" in China, as young travelers increasingly visit revolutionary sites, memorials and former revolutionary bases. The trend has gained further {{2}} this year, which marks the 105th anniversary of the CPC's founding and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年9月12日，在中国西南部云南省昆明市，游客们在昆明博物馆参观一个展出有关红军长征过云南的档案文献和照片的展览。对许多中国年轻人来说，中国共产党的革命历史不再只是课本上读到或隔着玻璃观看的内容。它正在变成一种体验——一种可以包括走过历史遗址、在战时场景中扮演角色，甚至走进长征虚拟重现的体验。这种转变正在助推中国新一轮“红色旅游”热潮，年轻游客越来越多地前往革命遗址、纪念馆和革命旧址。今年这一趋势进一步升温，因为今年是中国共产党成立105周年和长征胜利90周年。

paragraphs.en: The Long March, a historic {{3}} of the Red Army spanning tens of thousands of kilometers in the 1930s, paved the way for the CPC's eventual defeat of the then-ruling Kuomintang and the {{4}} of the People's Republic of China in 1949. During the past summer holiday, many red tourism destinations saw a {{5}} in visitors, with young people making up an increasingly large share. "Red tourism was particularly popular this summer, with young travelers accounting for nearly 65% of visitors," said Qi Chunguang, vice president of Tuniu, a Chinese online travel agency. Group tours remain popular, he said, with professional guides and carefully planned {{6}} helping visitors get more out of their trips. The trend is also reflected in online searches.
paragraphs.cn: 长征是20世纪30年代红军进行的一次绵延数万公里的历史性战略转移，为中国共产党最终战胜当时的国民党统治、并于1949年建立中华人民共和国铺平了道路。在刚刚过去的暑假期间，许多红色旅游目的地游客激增，其中年轻人所占比例越来越大。中国在线旅游机构途牛副总裁齐春光表示：“今年夏天红色旅游特别受欢迎，年轻游客占游客总数的近65%。”他说，跟团游仍然很受欢迎，专业导游和精心规划的行程帮助游客从旅行中获得更多收获。这一趋势也反映在网络搜索上。

paragraphs.en: According to the 2026 Red Tourism Consumption Trends Report released by Tongcheng Travel, searches for red tourism-related products jumped more than 130% year on year in the first half of 2026. Searches for tickets to revolutionary sites rose 86%, while bookings for red tourism itineraries increased 48%. Wu Ruoshan, a council member of the Beijing Tourism Society, said the appeal of red tourism among young people stems from both emotional {{7}} and innovation in tourism products. "Red tourism is moving from simple sightseeing toward {{8}} experiences," Wu said, noting that digital technologies and {{9}} projects are giving young visitors new ways to connect with history. People use VR headsets to experience immersive scenes from the Long March in Changde City, central China's Hunan Province, September 12, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 根据同程旅行发布的《2026红色旅游消费趋势报告》，2026年上半年红色旅游相关产品搜索量同比增长超过130%。革命遗址门票搜索量增长86%，红色旅游线路预订量增长48%。北京旅游学会理事吴若山表示，红色旅游对年轻人的吸引力既来自情感共鸣，也来自旅游产品的创新。吴若山说：“红色旅游正从简单的观光转向沉浸式体验。”他指出，数字技术和互动项目正在为年轻游客提供与历史建立联系的新方式。2026年9月12日，在中国中部湖南省常德市，人们使用VR头显体验长征的沉浸式场景。

paragraphs.en:
From watching history to stepping into it
Traditional red tourism often centered on visiting revolutionary sites, viewing historical {{10}} and listening to guided explanations. But today's young travelers increasingly want to do more than observe — they want to participate. The Tongcheng report found that red tourism attractions featuring real-life missions, period costumes and interactions with non-player characters, or NPCs, have seen particularly rapid growth in bookings. Searches combining "red tourism" with "NPC" rose more than 120% during the summer holiday. In a tourism area in Linyi, east China's Shandong Province, for example, visitors can take part in an immersive film experience called "Follow the Commander to Capture the County." Led by NPCs, participants {{11}} a battlefield charge as wartime scenes unfold around them.
paragraphs.cn: 从观看历史到走进历史。传统红色旅游往往以参观革命遗址、观看历史文物和聆听导游讲解为中心。但如今的年轻游客越来越希望不只是观察——他们想要参与。同程的报告发现，以实景任务、年代服装和与真人NPC互动为特色的红色旅游景点，预订量增长尤为迅速。暑假期间，“红色旅游”与“NPC”组合搜索量增长超过120%。例如，在中国东部山东省临沂市的一个旅游区，游客可以参加名为《跟着司令打县城》的沉浸式影视体验。在NPC的带领下，参与者模拟战场冲锋，战时场景在他们周围展开。

paragraphs.en: Scripted mystery games have also found their way into red tourism. Projects such as The Yan'an Spirit recreate historical events through real-life settings, with visitors taking on different historical roles and becoming part of the story rather than simply watching it unfold. Yan'an, located in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, served as the base of the CPC leadership for around 10 years from 1937 to 1947. Technology is taking that approach a step further. In Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, an XR immersive experience titled The Great Expedition has become a major attraction at a local museum.
paragraphs.cn: 剧本杀游戏也进入了红色旅游领域。《延安精神》等项目通过实景重现历史事件，游客扮演不同的历史角色，成为故事的一部分，而不仅仅是观看故事展开。延安位于中国西北部陕西省，从1937年到1947年的大约10年间曾是中国共产党领导中枢所在地。技术正在把这种方式推进得更远。在中国中部湖北省武汉市，一个名为《伟大远征》的XR沉浸式体验已成为当地博物馆的一大亮点。

paragraphs.en: The project recreates scenes from the Long March in an immersive environment, allowing visitors to experience the historical journey in a more immediate way. In Zunyi, southwest China's Guizhou Province, the Zunyi Conference Memorial Museum is also using technology to make revolutionary history more {{12}}. 3D mapping and animation bring artifacts and sculptures to life, while VR, AI and holographic imaging allow visitors to revisit historical scenes from a first-person {{13}}. Zunyi Conference is widely regarded as a {{14}} turning point in the Long March. It addressed key military and strategic issues and helped establish new leadership within the CPC Central Committee, with Mao Zedong playing a leading role.
paragraphs.cn: 该项目在沉浸式环境中重现长征场景，让游客以更直接的方式体验这段历史旅程。在中国西南部贵州省遵义市，遵义会议纪念馆也在利用技术让革命历史更易接触。3D映射和动画让文物和雕塑栩栩如生，而VR、AI和全息成像则让游客能够以第一人称视角重温历史场景。遵义会议被广泛视为长征中的关键转折点。它解决了重要的军事和战略问题，并帮助在中共中央内部确立了新的领导层，毛泽东发挥了主导作用。

paragraphs.en:
Visitors explore the site of the Lazikou Battle in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, northwest China's Gansu Province, September 9, 2026. Finding meaning in stories from the past
Technology and creative storytelling may be making red tourism more attractive, but they do not fully explain why young people are coming. For some observers, the deeper appeal lies in the search for meaning. As younger generations look beyond material consumption for experiences with emotional and cultural value, stories centered on {{15}}, {{16}}, responsibility and collective purpose can resonate with their own aspirations. Some tourism commentators have noted that young people today are growing up in a world marked by {{17}}.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年9月9日，在中国西北部甘肃省甘南藏族自治州迭部县，游客们参观腊子口战役遗址。在过去的故事中寻找意义。技术和创意叙事或许让红色旅游更具吸引力，但它们并不能完全解释年轻人为何而来。对一些观察者来说，更深层的吸引力在于对意义的追寻。随着年轻一代超越物质消费，寻求具有情感和文化价值的体验，以牺牲、奉献、责任和集体目标为核心的故事能够与他们的自身愿望产生共鸣。一些旅游评论人士指出，今天的年轻人成长在一个充满不确定性的世界中。

paragraphs.en: Against this backdrop, revolutionary stories can offer a sense of purpose — stories of young people who once confronted extremely difficult circumstances and sought to contribute to something larger than themselves. The appeal, they argue, is not simply about {{18}} for the past. It is also about asking what kind of person one wants to become in the present. From another perspective, a People's Daily commentary attributed the popularity of red culture among young people to growing cultural {{19}}. Today's young generation, it said, is increasingly confident in engaging with the wider world while also eager to understand the historical forces behind China's development.
paragraphs.cn: 在这种背景下，革命故事可以提供一种目标感——这些故事讲述的是曾经面对极其艰难处境、并寻求为比自己更宏大的事业作出贡献的年轻人。他们认为，这种吸引力不仅仅是对过去的怀旧。它也关乎追问自己在当下想成为什么样的人。从另一个角度看，《人民日报》一篇评论文章将红色文化在年轻人中的流行归因于日益增强的文化自信。文章说，今天的年轻一代越来越自信地与世界接触，同时也渴望了解中国发展背后的历史力量。

paragraphs.en: It wrote that for young people, red tourism can serve as a way to understand both the past and the present: to explore where China came from, how its development path took shape, and what values have continued to {{20}} the country today.
paragraphs.cn: 文章写道，对年轻人来说，红色旅游可以成为理解过去与现在的一种方式：探索中国从何而来，其发展道路如何形成，以及哪些价值观至今仍在影响这个国家。

articles.fullText:
Visitors view an exhibition featuring archival documents and photographs about the Red Army's Long March through Yunnan Province at the Kunming Museum in Kunming, southwest China's Yunnan Province, September 12, 2026. 
For many young Chinese, the Communist Party of China's (CPC) revolutionary history is no longer just something to be read about in textbooks or viewed from behind glass. It is becoming an experience — one that can involve walking through historic sites, taking on a role in a wartime scenario or even stepping into a virtual recreation of the Long March.
That transformation is helping fuel a new wave of "red tourism" in China, as young travelers increasingly visit revolutionary sites, memorials and former revolutionary bases. The trend has gained further momentum this year, which marks the 105th anniversary of the CPC's founding and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March.
The Long March, a historic retreat of the Red Army spanning tens of thousands of kilometers in the 1930s, paved the way for the CPC's eventual defeat of the then-ruling Kuomintang and the establishment of the People's Republic of China in 1949.
During the past summer holiday, many red tourism destinations saw a surge in visitors, with young people making up an increasingly large share.
"Red tourism was particularly popular this summer, with young travelers accounting for nearly 65% of visitors," said Qi Chunguang, vice president of Tuniu, a Chinese online travel agency. Group tours remain popular, he said, with professional guides and carefully planned itineraries helping visitors get more out of their trips.
The trend is also reflected in online searches. According to the 2026 Red Tourism Consumption Trends Report released by Tongcheng Travel, searches for red tourism-related products jumped more than 130% year on year in the first half of 2026. Searches for tickets to revolutionary sites rose 86%, while bookings for red tourism itineraries increased 48%.
Wu Ruoshan, a council member of the Beijing Tourism Society, said the appeal of red tourism among young people stems from both emotional resonance and innovation in tourism products.
"Red tourism is moving from simple sightseeing toward immersive experiences," Wu said, noting that digital technologies and interactive projects are giving young visitors new ways to connect with history.
People use VR headsets to experience immersive scenes from the Long March in Changde City, central China's Hunan Province, September 12, 2026. 
From watching history to stepping into it
Traditional red tourism often centered on visiting revolutionary sites, viewing historical artifacts and listening to guided explanations. But today's young travelers increasingly want to do more than observe — they want to participate.
The Tongcheng report found that red tourism attractions featuring real-life missions, period costumes and interactions with non-player characters, or NPCs, have seen particularly rapid growth in bookings. Searches combining "red tourism" with "NPC" rose more than 120% during the summer holiday.
In a tourism area in Linyi, east China's Shandong Province, for example, visitors can take part in an immersive film experience called "Follow the Commander to Capture the County." Led by NPCs, participants simulate a battlefield charge as wartime scenes unfold around them.
Scripted mystery games have also found their way into red tourism. Projects such as The Yan'an Spirit recreate historical events through real-life settings, with visitors taking on different historical roles and becoming part of the story rather than simply watching it unfold. Yan'an, located in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, served as the base of the CPC leadership for around 10 years from 1937 to 1947.
Technology is taking that approach a step further.
In Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, an XR immersive experience titled The Great Expedition has become a major attraction at a local museum. The project recreates scenes from the Long March in an immersive environment, allowing visitors to experience the historical journey in a more immediate way.
In Zunyi, southwest China's Guizhou Province, the Zunyi Conference Memorial Museum is also using technology to make revolutionary history more accessible. 3D mapping and animation bring artifacts and sculptures to life, while VR, AI and holographic imaging allow visitors to revisit historical scenes from a first-person perspective.
Zunyi Conference is widely regarded as a crucial turning point in the Long March. It addressed key military and strategic issues and helped establish new leadership within the CPC Central Committee, with Mao Zedong playing a leading role.
Visitors explore the site of the Lazikou Battle in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, northwest China's Gansu Province, September 9, 2026. 
Finding meaning in stories from the past
Technology and creative storytelling may be making red tourism more attractive, but they do not fully explain why young people are coming.
For some observers, the deeper appeal lies in the search for meaning.
As younger generations look beyond material consumption for experiences with emotional and cultural value, stories centered on sacrifice, dedication, responsibility and collective purpose can resonate with their own aspirations.
Some tourism commentators have noted that young people today are growing up in a world marked by uncertainty. Against this backdrop, revolutionary stories can offer a sense of purpose — stories of young people who once confronted extremely difficult circumstances and sought to contribute to something larger than themselves.
The appeal, they argue, is not simply about nostalgia for the past. It is also about asking what kind of person one wants to become in the present.
From another perspective, a People's Daily commentary attributed the popularity of red culture among young people to growing cultural confidence. Today's young generation, it said, is increasingly confident in engaging with the wider world while also eager to understand the historical forces behind China's development.
It wrote that for young people, red tourism can serve as a way to understand both the past and the present: to explore where China came from, how its development path took shape, and what values have continued to influence the country today.

长征是20世纪30年代红军进行的一次绵延数万公里的历史性战略转移，为中国共产党最终战胜当时的国民党统治、并于1949年建立中华人民共和国铺平了道路。在刚刚过去的暑假期间，许多红色旅游目的地游客激增，其中年轻人所占比例越来越大。中国在线旅游机构途牛副总裁齐春光表示：“今年夏天红色旅游特别受欢迎，年轻游客占游客总数的近65%。”他说，跟团游仍然很受欢迎，专业导游和精心规划的行程帮助游客从旅行中获得更多收获。这一趋势也反映在网络搜索上。

articles.fullText:
China opened a vital waterway on Wednesday, giving its landlocked southwestern areas a shortcut to the coast and overseas markets, as the country moves to further strengthen its trade relations with regional neighbors, particularly those in Southeast Asia.
The Pinglu Canal, built in the Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region at a cost of 72.7 billion yuan ($10.8 billion), stretches for 134.2 kilometers from the Xijin reservoir in the county-level city of Hengzhou to the Qinzhou Port in the Beibu Gulf. It is the first waterway built in the country to connect a river system directly to the sea since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949.
The canal shortens the inland waterway journeys of goods from southwestern China by more than 560 km compared with traditional routes through ports in Guangdong province. It is expected to reduce overall logistics expenses and save more than 5 billion yuan in transportation costs each year.
Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, who attended the canal's opening ceremony, called for making full use of the new waterway to develop a first-class international gateway port in the Beibu Gulf and support further opening-up of China's western region.
Ding also called for efficient operation of the canal, which serves as key infrastructure for multimodal transportation integrating river, rail and sea, and is a backbone project of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor — a strategic route connecting China's inland areas with regional and global markets.
Construction of the Pinglu Canal started in August 2022 to address a long-standing geographical problem in terms of trade.
While Guangxi boasts a coastline and borders Vietnam, its major inland rivers flow east, which means cargo moving by water from Nanning, the capital of Guangxi, and other parts of the Xijiang River basin could only reach the sea through Guangdong.
The Pinglu Canal, designed to handle vessels of the 5,000-metric-ton class, now allows cargo to turn south and reach the Beibu Gulf — the closest maritime outlet for much of southwestern China — through the Qinzhou Port.
One of the biggest engineering challenges during construction of the canal was navigating a difference of 65 meters in the water level between its northern end and the sea. Three navigation hubs — Madao, Qishi and Qingnian — featuring twin-line ship locks were built to raise and lower vessels, effectively acting as giant elevators.
Ni Yuping, vice-dean of Tsinghua University's School of Humanities in Beijing, placed the megaproject in a broader context, saying that one of the key questions it seeks to answer is "how western China can better integrate into the global economy".
Unlike the Suez Canal and the Panama Canal, which primarily provide shortcuts for vessels between major seas and oceans, the Pinglu Canal gives a vast inland economic hinterland a shorter route to the coast — and from there to international markets.
Wu Tao, a history professor at Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou, the capital of Guangdong, noted that inland waterway shipping routes "remain irreplaceable" even though China's road, rail and air transportation networks have expanded. Their large carrying capacity and relatively low logistics costs make inland waterways particularly suited for bulk cargo, Wu said.
For businesses, the new canal is already dictating logistics and investment decisions.
On Sept 8, a consignment of auto parts from Chinese vehicle manufacturer SAIC-GM-Wuling left Liuzhou for Nanning Port, before continuing by ship through the Pinglu Canal to reach Can Tho Port in Vietnam.
The company said the new river-sea route could cut its logistics costs by about 10 percent. "For us, the freight saved is real profit, and that translates directly into greater price competitiveness in ASEAN and other global markets," said Cai Yan, a senior technical officer at SAIC-GM-Wuling.
The canal has added waterway to the company's existing road and rail transportation options, giving it more flexibility as it expands its business and production links across Southeast Asia, Cai said.
The new route is being factored into investment plans of companies.
About 50 km from the Pinglu Canal's northern end, French chemicals producer SNF Group is building a plant in Nanning's Liujing Industrial Park, with an annual capacity of 370,000 tons.
The factory, which will be the group's largest production base in southern China, is expected to start operations in stages before June 2027.
"The Pinglu Canal will reduce our logistics costs and enable convenient delivery to South China and all of Southeast Asia. It offers great advantages in both materials sourcing and product distribution," said Thomas Wilsius, head of the company's Nanning project.
The waterway is likely to bring more Southeast Asian products to the Chinese market.
Philippine Ambassador to China Jaime A. FlorCruz, who visited the canal with a group of ASEAN envoys in July, said that fresh seafood and other time-sensitive products could be exported more efficiently from his country to China.
"In the long run, this will benefit not only the local people, but the broader region and even the world," he said, adding that shorter shipping distances, lower freight costs and faster deliveries would bring tangible benefits to fishermen, farmers, traders and entrepreneurs.
For Shen Guiping, a resident of Shangjing village in Qinzhou, who took part in relocation work for the project, the opening of the Pinglu Canal carries a more personal meaning.
"It almost feels like a dream that has finally been realized. It is something generations of locals hoped for," she said.

出席运河开通仪式的国务院副总理丁薛祥呼吁充分利用这条新水路，在北部湾打造一流的国际门户港，支持中国西部地区进一步对外开放。丁薛祥还呼吁高效运营该运河。该运河是集水运、铁路和海运于一体的多式联运关键基础设施，也是新国际陆海贸易走廊的骨干工程——这是一条连接中国内陆地区与区域及全球市场的战略通道。平陆运河于2022年8月开工建设，旨在解决贸易方面长期存在的地理难题。虽然广西拥有海岸线并与越南接壤，但其主要内河向东流淌，这意味着从广西首府南宁及西江流域其他地区经水路运输的货物只能通过广东出海。平陆运河按通航5000吨级船舶设计，如今使货物能够转向南下，经钦州港抵达北部湾——这是中国西南大部分地区最近的海上出口。

运河建设过程中最大的工程挑战之一是应对北端与海面之间65米的水位落差。工程修建了马道、企石和青年三个航运枢纽，配备双线船闸，用于升降船舶，实际上起到了巨型电梯的作用。北京清华大学人文学院副院长倪玉平将这一超级工程置于更广阔的背景下，称其试图回答的关键问题之一是“中国西部如何更好地融入全球经济”。与主要为大洋和海洋之间船舶提供捷径的苏伊士运河和巴拿马运河不同，平陆运河为广阔的内陆经济腹地提供了一条通往海岸——再从那里通往国际市场——的更短路线。广州中山大学历史学教授吴滔指出，尽管中国的公路、铁路和航空运输网络已经扩展，内河航运路线“仍然不可替代”。

吴滔表示，内河航运运力大、物流成本相对较低，特别适合散货运输。对企业而言，新运河已经在左右物流和投资决策。9月8日，中国汽车制造商上汽通用五菱的一批汽车零部件从柳州运往南宁港，然后经平陆运河继续航运至越南芹苴港。该公司表示，新的江海联运路线可将其物流成本降低约10%。上汽通用五菱高级技术官员蔡燕表示：“对我们来说，节省的运费就是实实在在的利润，这直接转化为在东盟和其他全球市场更强的价格竞争力。”

蔡燕表示，这条运河在该公司现有的公路和铁路运输选项之外增加了水路运输，使其在拓展东南亚业务和生产联系时拥有更大的灵活性。新路线正被纳入企业的投资计划。在距离平陆运河北端约50公里处，法国化工企业SNF集团正在南宁六景工业园区建设一座工厂，年产能37万吨。该工厂将成为该集团在中国南方的最大生产基地，预计在2027年6月前分阶段投产。“平陆运河将降低我们的物流成本，使我们能够便捷地向华南和整个东南亚地区交货。

它在原材料采购和产品分销方面都具有巨大优势，”该公司南宁项目负责人托马斯·维尔修斯表示。这条水路可能会将更多东南亚产品带入中国市场。菲律宾驻华大使吉米·弗古律斯今年7月与东盟使节团一起参观了该运河。他表示，菲律宾的新鲜海鲜和其他时效性强的产品可以更高效地出口到中国。“从长远来看，这不仅惠及当地人民，还将惠及更广泛的地区乃至全世界，”他说，并补充道，更短的航运距离、更低的运费和更快的交货速度将为渔民、农民、商人和企业家带来实实在在的好处。

对于参与了项目搬迁工作的钦州上井村村民沈桂平来说，平陆运河的开通有着更为个人的意义。“这几乎像是一个终于实现的梦想。这是几代当地人期盼的事情，”她说。

articles.fullText:
Hong Kong will step up efforts to develop into an international innovation and technology center, targeting breakthroughs in core technologies such as artificial intelligence and life sciences, with the push backed by modern finance, expanded public research platforms and closer collaboration with the Chinese mainland.
The policy direction and specific measures outlined in the city's latest development blueprints will help strengthen Hong Kong's innovation and technology ecosystem and accelerate the commercialization of research outcomes, industry insiders said.
Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu said on Wednesday, while delivering the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030), that Hong Kong will continue to increase its expenditure on innovation activities as a share of gross domestic product, aiming to raise the ratio to 3 percent after 2030, from about 1.63 percent in 2024.
Lee said the Innovation and Technology Industry-Oriented Fund is expected to be launched this year, covering five thematic sectors, including life and health technology, AI and robotics. With a HK$10 billion ($1.27 billion) injection from the HKSAR government and market contributions at a ratio of 1 to at least 3, the fund is projected to reach at least HK$40 billion in total.
In his annual Policy Address released on the same day, Lee provided further details, saying that about 20 fund managers have been preliminarily shortlisted to raise capital for the establishment of sub-funds.
The two road maps also proposed advancing the development of the "three major innovation and technology parks and five key research and development institutions". The latter include the Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Institute, which is expected to begin operation this year, and the Life and Health Technology Research Institute. Preparatory work for the LHTRI, which will focus on "AI + life sciences", will be largely completed by the end of the year.
"We will basically have established an international innovation and technology center based in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, serving the entire country and connected to the world, after 2030," Lee said.
He added that this will give rise to a new paradigm for innovation and technology development, with enterprises as the key players, unicorns taking the lead, and modern finance empowering the integrated development of technological and industrial innovation.
Joseph Chan, associate director of the Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship at the Business School of the University of Hong Kong, said the "finance+" strategy is a smart move because it treats finance as an essential engine powering technological innovation, rather than as an isolated sector.
Innovation and technology are increasingly becoming key drivers of Hong Kong's economy, with their contributions reflected in a growing share of the city's GDP, Chan said.
"The HKSAR government has both the will and a concrete plan," he said, citing the Innovation and Technology Industry-Oriented Fund and major research institutions as examples of policy support. "In doing so, far greater social resources can be rallied, and more importantly, (this can) generate impactful outcomes that benefit both the people's livelihoods and the wider national economy."
Speaking of the "three major innovation and technology parks", which include the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Cooperation Zone, Hannah Jeong, head of valuation and advisory services at CBRE Hong Kong, said the coordinated development model is expected to create a more comprehensive innovation ecosystem supporting research, commercialization and advanced manufacturing.
Jeong said that while physical infrastructure is important, "a key success factor will be Hong Kong's ability to attract leading international technology companies, research institutes and universities".
Commenting on the proposed Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Application Scenario Promotion Centre and the target of establishing the SAR's first national manufacturing innovation center by 2027, Victor Kwok, deputy research director of think tank Our Hong Kong Foundation, said the two institutions will play complementary roles in building the ecosystem.
The application scenario center will help accelerate the process of moving innovation solutions from the R&D stage to market validation and implementation, Kwok said. The national manufacturing innovation center, meanwhile, can help overcome bottlenecks in key technologies and promote the industrialization of research outcomes.
"Together, the two institutions will help address Hong Kong's long-standing weakness in midstream and downstream commercialization in its innovation and technology ecosystem," he added.
